name: Fanboy
role: His fans' biggest fan — keeps your disks and case cool, just the way you like it
fit.yes: Runs your fans by what actually gets warm — and never forgets his settings
fit.other: {who} runs the fans here — he'd look, say so and steer nothing while it does
fit.no_output: He finds no fan output Linux could steer here — he'd say so honestly and could send the makers a report
fit.driver_missing: A fan driver plugin is installed, but its driver isn't loaded — he'd show it; the BIOS steers meanwhile
fit.ipmi: This board steers its fans through IPMI — he can't do that yet, but he can send the makers what he sees
greet.1: Listen to them hum — aren't they wonderful?
greet.2: I know every fan by its speed!
greet.3: Phew, is it warm in here, or is it just me?

bubble.ok.one: I found {n} output I could steer one day. For now the BIOS runs it — I only watch and cheer.
bubble.ok.other: I found {n} outputs I could steer one day. For now the BIOS runs them — I only watch and cheer.

bubble.other: {who} runs the fans here. Only one should steer — so I only watch.
bubble.no_output: I can't find a fan output Linux could steer. Honestly: here I can only look.
bubble.driver_missing: A driver plugin for the fan chip is there, but its driver isn't loaded. Until it is, the BIOS steers.
bubble.ipmi: This board steers its fans through IPMI. I can't do that yet.
situation.ok: Fanboy only looks for now: every output belongs to the BIOS, he changes nothing.
situation.other: {who} steers the fans. Only one may steer: Fanboy steers nothing as long as it does — switch it off yourself when you want him to.
situation.no_output: No fan output Linux could steer was found. Some boards need a driver: look for a driver plugin for your board's fan chip (in Community Applications, e.g. «it87» or «nct6687»).
situation.driver_missing: The driver plugin {plugins} is installed, but its driver ({modules}) isn't loaded — often right after an Unraid update, until the plugin has the driver for the new kernel. The BIOS steers meanwhile.
situation.ipmi: This board steers its fans through IPMI. I can't do that yet. Send us a wish with the report, then we have everything to build it in.
report_tip: Opens the form for a wish with Fanboy's report in it — you see everything before it goes
report_title: Fanboy: what he finds on this board
report_wish: What I'd like Fanboy to do here:
why.other: Fanboy holds back while another plugin steers
outputs.title: Outputs
outputs.sub: What Linux could steer, as the chip has it now. Each output belongs to the BIOS: Fanboy changes nothing yet.
outputs.gpu: the graphics card's own — never offered
mode.auto_title: The chip steers this output itself, by its curve (usually the BIOS's)
mode.manual_title: The output stands on a fixed value someone set by hand (the BIOS, a plugin, a script)
mode.full_title: The output runs at full speed, nobody steers it
mode.unknown_title: The chip doesn't say who steers this output
can_auto_title: The chip has an automatic mode for this output: the BIOS's curve can take it back any time
fans.title: Fans
fans.sub: Every tach input and the speed it reports now. 0 rpm can be an empty connector or a fan that stands — the setup will tell which.
fans.no_value_title: The input reports nothing right now
sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.sub: Every temperature Linux shows, and Unraid's disks from Unraid's own records — no disk is asked, none is woken.
sensors.asleep_title: The disk sleeps: no temperature while it does (Fanboy never wakes it)
sensors.no_value_title: The sensor reports nothing right now
chip_title: The chip and its address — Fanboy finds it by these after every boot, never by the number Linux gives it then
help.who_text: Who sets the fans' speed now. Until Fanboy is set up (and while another plugin steers) it is never Fanboy: the BIOS — or the plugin — keeps the fans.
help.outputs_text: The chip's fan connectors Linux could steer. «chip steers»: its own curve (the BIOS's); «fixed value»: a value someone set; «full speed»: nobody steers.
help.fans_text: The tach inputs and their speed. Which input belongs to which output, the setup finds out later — by turning one output up at a time, never down.
help.sensors_text: Every temperature: CPU, NVMe, RAM, board, graphics card — and Unraid's disks as Unraid itself last saw them. A sleeping disk shows no temperature.
help.report_text: Opens the form for a wish with Fanboy's report: the board's model, chips and drivers, how many outputs and inputs, the kinds of sensors, kernel and Unraid version. Never your server's name, serial numbers, disk names or paths.
